peer_results.rationale: No candidate was substantively comparable. AMD's candidate D068 concerns the acquisition of Pensando (a business combination) and D142 concerns the auditor's opinion. Neither involves the sale of a non-controlling interest in a semiconductor co-investment program or the specific recognition of proceeds in capital in excess of par value related to a VIE stake sale as disclosed by Intel.

No candidate was substantively comparable. Broadcom's candidates D120 and D016 both concern a ten-for-one forward stock split. A stock split adjusts share counts and authorized capital but does not involve the sale of an interest in a specific entity (like Ireland SCIP) to a third party (like Apollo) for net proceeds, nor does it involve the same VIE consolidation and operating rights dynamics.

comparisons.peer_summary: Treasury stock is carried at cost. When treasury stock is retired, any excess of the repurchase price over par value is allocated between additional capital and retained earnings.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose accounting treatments involving 'capital in excess of par value' or 'additional capital' derived from capital transactions, though the drivers differ. Intel recognizes $11.0 billion in proceeds from the sale of a non-controlling interest as an increase to capital in excess of par value. Micron discloses its general policy for treasury stock retirement, where the excess of the repurchase price over par value is allocated to additional capital. Both highlight the mechanical flow of capital adjustments relative to par value, but Intel's represents a significant external equity event while Micron's describes standard share repurchase accounting.

sentences.text: In the second quarter of 2024, we closed a transaction with Apollo Global Management, Inc. (Apollo) involving the sale of 49% of our interest in an Irish limited liability company (Ireland SCIP) for net proceeds of $11.0 billion, which increased our capital in excess of par value.
When we retire our treasury stock, any excess of the repurchase price paid over par value is allocated between additional capital and retained earnings.
